note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/screen100/{base_cue,sft025_cue,sft05_cue,sft1_cue}-01/per_problem.json (committed; 100 rows each, one per problem_index, fields problem_index, score_v3, cap_hit (bool), n_generated). First row per problem_index kept; cap_hit counted only when exactly true. D is an integer difference of counts. Interval: bootstrap over the union of problem_index values, each entry the tuple of the four arms' rows (None where absent), D recomputed per resample. Ambiguity: the recipe is explicit; alt_measured counts a cap hit as n_generated >= 16,384 instead of the stored cap_hit flag, in case the flag and the length disagree. A row that stopped for another reason at exactly 16,384 or a flag set by a different rule would make the two differ. D is a difference of maxima, so its bootstrap interval is biased upward (max of noisy counts).

Files: wsp1/screen100 base_cue-01, sft025_cue-01, sft1_cue-01 per_problem.json. First row per problem_index, restricted to problem_index in all three (100 expected). M(arm) = median n_generated over rows with cap_hit not true and n_generated numeric (null/missing cap_hit treated as not a cap hit, i.e. kept as finished); even count -> mean of the two middle values. f undefined (M(sft1) <= M(base) or a median missing) -> refuted_without_number. Bootstrap over common problems (tuple of 3 rows), medians recomputed per resample; an undefined resample is set to -inf (counts as refuted), which would show as -Infinity in the interval if it happens. Ambiguity: each arm's median uses its own finished rows, so the three medians are over different problem sets (problems the base or sft025 fails to finish are dropped from that arm only); alt_measured uses only problems finished in all three arms (paired). Selection effect: if sft025 caps on long problems, its finished median is pulled down, lowering f.

Files: wsp1/screen100 sft1_cue-01, sft025_cue-01, sft05_cue-01 per_problem.json. First row per problem_index. m = median of n_generated over all kept sft1_cue rows including cap hits at 16,384 (rows with non-numeric n_generated would be excluded from m and from S; none expected). S = sft1 problems with n_generated <= m (ties at m are in S). Pooled cap-hit rows: sft025 and sft05 kept rows with cap_hit exactly true and problem_index present in sft1_cue; a problem capped in both arms counts twice. Statistic = pooled rows in S / all pooled rows; zero pooled rows -> refuted_without_number. Bootstrap over sft1 problems (tuple of sft1, sft025, sft05 rows), with m recomputed per resample; a resample with no pooled cap hits is set to +inf (counts as refuted). Ambiguity: alt_measured counts each problem once if it is capped in either intermediate arm (problem-level share rather than row-level). Another reading not computed: m over sft1 finished rows only, which would shift the short/long split down. With few cap hits (likely under ~15 rows) the share is coarse and the interval wide.
